messages:
Jordan Li: FYI seeing a backlog of 1-GPU jobs in us-west1b this morning. Lots of Pending -> FailedScheduling even though cluster shows free GPU capacity. Feels like topologySpread + scheduler scoring are colliding with our binpack goals.
Priya Kumar: can you paste one of the `kubectl describe pod` events?
Jordan Li: pasted one below:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   1m    default-scheduler  0/30 nodes are available: 8 node(s) had taint {gpu:NoSchedule}, 6 node(s) had insufficient resources, 10 node(s) failed predicate, 6 node(s) MatchNodeSelector failed.
  Normal   NotTriggerScaleUp  30s   cluster-autoscaler  Pod fits but scale-up was not triggered
```
Jordan Li: the "failed predicate" here maps to our custom topology affinity check that rejects nodes if placing this pod would increase rack spread beyond threshold.
Nikhil Rao: ah right, SCHED-5102 changed the spread plugin weight to prefer even rack distribution to avoid hot racks. That was meant for large batch jobs but now tiny 1-GPU interactive jobs are being spread widely leaving 1-GPU holes.
Priya Kumar: which nodes are showing allocatable GPUs? Could be that some nodes have fractional MIG reservations making them look free but actually not match request.
Jordan Li: quick `kubectl get nodes -o wide` snippet: `node-a (rack-1) allocatable: 1 GPU, node-b (rack-1) allocatable: 0, node-c (rack-2) allocatable: 1, node-d (rack-2) allocatable: 2` — scheduler keeps alternating across racks due to spread scoring and then pods land on nodes w/ taint or insufficient ephemeral storage and fail.
infra-bot: Alert: scheduler rollout sched-2026-03-19-v3 completed 2026-03-19T03:14Z in us-west1 region. See changelog.
Claire Ramos: we intentionally increased spread weight to prevent >70% GPU utilization on a single rack after last thermal incident. But for workloads with many 1-GPU tasks that's counterproductive.
Nikhil Rao: options: 1) change spread weight to be conditional by pod size (only apply for pods requesting >=4 GPUs), 2) add a binpack filter that prefers nodes with existing GPU allocations (preferSameNode), 3) introduce a topology-aware packing plugin that tries to fill GPUs inside racks before spreading.
Priya Kumar: quick risk note: packing increases intra-rack thermal and egress risk, but spreading increases fragmentation and higher overall evictions/cold-starts which are worse for latency-sensitive workloads. Need a balance.
Jordan Li: I can prototype a conditional weighting rule in the scheduler config (if nvidia.com/gpu < 2 then spread_weight = 0) and do a canary on us-west1b-rack-2.
ops-oncall: willing to run canary. Suggest also adding a short admission-controller gate that allows 1-GPU pods to preempt low-priority backlog on same rack for 5m during canary.
Nikhil Rao: also add a telemetry check: track "tiny-pod packing ratio" (fraction of 1-GPU pods placed on partially-filled nodes) and eviction rate. We had no metric for that.
Claire Ramos: put the config change behind a feature flag and add a fallback to previous behavior if eviction rate rises >5% in 15m window.
Jordan Li: created SCHED-5177 for the conditional spread change and linked to existing ticket SCHED-5102. I'll push a canary plan in the ticket.
Priya Kumar: once canary is stable, let's bake an e2e test: simulate 200 concurrent 1-GPU pods + intermittent node-level disk pressure to ensure we don't accidentally create matchNodeSelector misses.
ops-oncall: starting canary in us-west1b-rack-2 now. Will report back at +10m and +30m with eviction and schedule success counts.
Jordan Li: thanks. Posting followup in #incidents if anything spikes. :eyes:
